finite.et: The adjective is derived from Middle English fynyte, finit, from Latin fīnītus, perfect passive participle of fīniō (“to finish; to terminate”), from fīnis (“boundary”). The word displaced Old English ġeendodlīċ. The noun is derived from the adjective.

s.d: Strict and dictatorial, exercising firm ruthless control.
e: I couldn't believe that iron-handed old tyrant would have a son waho cared for nothing but praying.

iron-handed.et: From the idea of having an iron hand.

righteous among the nations.et: Translation of Hebrew חסיד אומות העולם / חֲסִיד אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (khasíd 'umót ha'olám, literally “righteous [one] of the nations of the world”).
